chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washsha', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whatever the rope severs from it, it is dead; and whatever you find of its remaining body alive, slaughter it.

key_terms.الْحِبَالَةُ: The rope, net, or catching device used to secure the animal.
key_terms.فَذَكِّهِ: Slaughter it; the imperative to perform the ritual slaughter on the remaining living part.
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: Dead; indicating the part is not ritually slaughtered and thus not halal for consumption without further processing.

ai.seo_question: How do you determine if a caught animal is halal if part of it was severed by the net or rope?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'partial death' in aquatic creatures, distinguishing between limbs severed by the catching tool (which are inedible) and the surviving torso (which requires ritual slaughter). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the method of capture determines the state of death, ensuring that only the living portion is consecrated through *dhakka* for consumption.
